questions.prompt: Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm using Heron’s formula, to 1 decimal place.

questions.prompt: A triangular park has sides 50 m, 120 m and 130 m. Find its area in m².
Explain the steps you would use to find the area of a four-sided field ABCD if you can only measure lengths.
questions.modelAnswer: Measure the four sides and one diagonal, say AC. This splits the field into two triangles, ABC and ACD, with all sides known. Find each area with Heron’s formula (s = half the perimeter, then √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]), and add the two areas.
rubric: Measure a diagonal to split into triangles
questions.explain: Criterion D: planning a real measurement.
